notes.title: Football Drama “HD” — Major Update Released!

You can now update Football Drama and get a full-featured version built for desktops: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33228816/1143d797a4ec5153d1ac6f3a48e9577823ebb383.gif[/img]

Last but not least, Steam Winter Sale is coming...

This option also removes the enter fields animations and the replays.

We have a new “night mode” - some matches are played in the evenings. We also introduced some post-processing for the graphics of the whole application, and you can see both effects in action here:

We recap three months of sales and preview Football Drama expansions: "HD" version, Switch porting, expanded narrative, Japanese localization.

We released Football Drama on [b]September 18[/b], releasing on Steam and mobile. We sold over 6000 units up to now, we have a constant stream of sales, and we got some very nice press ːsteamhappyː

We are happy to put it in this Winter Sale, and on the 23rd of December we will also publish a free demo of the mobile version on iOS ([url=https://apps.apple.com/app/football-drama/id1401903505]full iOS version here[/url]).

[previewyoutube=9PbjoDzvPgI;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Match Card Analysis, Shameless Pundits, Slo-mo Replays...
notes.notes:
This update is "major" because we improved several aspects of the game also in consequence of the feedback received.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33228816/27d80753753d23eafa81ca48459a8803872ea5d4.jpg[/img]

The main updates are:
[list]
[*] After every training and for each successful card played, you get detailed feedback about your team's state compared with your current opponent. This is something several players requested. This reveals a lot of background, so we tried to make it so that it does not "break the magic" of how matches go.

[*] We introduced more variations in the narrative (e.g. press meetings), with more integration between matches and Rocco's life, and removed some end of match loops ("handshakegate") after the first championship weeks.
[/list]

Other improvements:
[list]
[*] Action replays improved a lot; moreover, you can close replays way sooner just by tapping on them.
[*] Improved the AI on some match actions.
[*] Minor font size issues in non-English versions.
[/list]

Specifically for the mobile version: if you play it on a high-resolution tablet, you can play it in landscape mode, getting the additional features available on HD layouts (Football Drama is also available on iOS  and Android).

And finally, the Autumn Steam sale should go live really really soon... :-)

notes.title: Unknown Pleasures: The only game in the office
notes.notes:
The office is eerily empty tonight, as RPS has vanquished another foe, and been locked out in turn by my guerrilla forces. I am alone in the building. There is only me, Candide the rainbow llama, and the endless invisible stream of code I must consume to sustain my terrible power.

It is time, my friends, for Unknown Pleasures, our regular delivery of the best lesser-known games on Steam, direct to your eyeballs, or possibly your earcubes. Installing malware on every PC I find left on overnight this week: island escapes, imperial collapses, and forbidden studies.

(more…)

notes.title: Have a productive weekend: Football Drama culture test!
notes.notes:
[b]This weekend don't waste your time with your family and friends, or learning something useful; focus on useless football notions, and take our test![/b]

So you see this table here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33228816/45eae9c641676fe8453d814e72f9cd34ed39d58b.jpg[/img]

[url=https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/448879427817046016/627121462423060492/Artboard_13x-100.jpg](Here you find the image full size.)[/url]

These are the teams, managers, supporters and towns you find in Football Drama.
Now, none of these officially refers to anything real. [b]But to your overexcited mind, what teams, managers stadiums and supporters are we mocking?[/b]

To be even more sure that you didn't miss anything and that the whole thing takes an absurd amount of wasted time, we assigned little numbers to the cells, even to the empty ones! Also this way we may actually make it deciphering your answers.

Send us your answers to games@open-lab.com by Monday morning 10 CET (September 30th) and to the one who gets most of them right... I mean that we "like", we'll send a free code for either Steam, Android or iOS, as the winner wishes. 

[b]Say no to family & friends! Research the dark corners of football, today![/b]

notes.title: First Football Drama Update: Speed Up!
notes.notes:
So we just went live with our first Football Drama update. 

We are sorry for the two bugs, they would not have occurred if we had a cross platform cross language testing team, but being two guys that try to do everything (marketing and support too) we do what we can. So THANKS for the users who reported them in detail so we could fix them. 
Football Drama is also doing very well on mobile, on [url=https://apps.apple.com/app/football-drama/id1401903505]App Store (iOS)[/url] and [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.openlab.footballdrama]Google Play (Android)[/url], thanks for that too.

These are the improvements/changes/fixes:
[list]
[*] We added a tutorial step in the second half to tell about the "tap or click in the field centre" just after you made a choice in the match that speeds up the whole thing. For players that like faster matches, it changes the whole feeling of the game.
[*] We removed the (sometimes repetitive) meeting with the president when nothing crucial is happening (i.e. he is not furious, you are not fired, you didn't win the championship). This too seems a small change but makes the whole flow more natural.
[*] We did a lot of improvements in the translation, in particular in French (Charlene Lebrun), Italian (Luca Papale), Chinese (Melanie Luo), Russian.
[*] BUG FIX: We fixed a bug in the rendering of the German and Russian Oracle dialogue that crashed the game.
[*] BUG FIX: There was an occasional problem in saving the state of matches (not involving you) of the current week.
[/list]
So we hope you enjoy the game even more \o/

notes.title: Football Drama is a management game with personality
notes.notes:
Football Drama is out now.

You’re the new manager of a struggling football team – they’re all fictional, thankfully – and must survive the season. Not the team (although winning matches obviously helps), but you. It’s pretty weird. I sorta like it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33228816/87b2faae18535666a221e9f028707f406f808fef.png[/img]

Football Drama will be released on Steam for Windows and Mac (also on mobile) this week on Wednesday 18th. First week with 15% discount, also soundtrack & bundle available. 

Evaluation keys are available now, write to games@open-lab.com.

In Football Drama, you’re Rocco Galliano, the existentially troubled manager of a struggling football team. Train players, survive the drama, choose your own narrative, and play turn-based football matches via hard choices and special cards. If you avoid the axe you could win the championship, understand what is football, retire at the French Riviera, end up in jail, or who knows what else!

Football Drama is a narrative game with choices, that generates cards and power to be used in fast turn-based matches as part of a football championship. In match controls allow to always pick between safe and risky choices, balancing team conditions.

notes.title: The Wave That Carries The Underdog
notes.notes:
One of the reasons for football fascination is that the underdog always has a chance. How could we model that in an algorithm without recurring to randomness? 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/6668620f376c0c08a10f733c5b9a50297c085a66.jpg[/img]

In Football Drama we used wave functions of different widths (corresponding to the differences between the two teams), that oscillate with different periods.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/6fb2981ceb9f2a73c635cecb443d6e373fc3bb87.jpg[/img]

(From [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave#/media/File:Superpositionprinciple.gif]Wikipedia[/url].)

This models the fact that in no football match the stronger team dominates *all the time*. There are two waves that are composed with basic powers to give current strength.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/c574902bded411015ea2cb63405bd698be9c5280.jpg[/img]

So if the underdog strikes when his wave is high and the opponent’s low…

notes.title: Football Drama's Modding Plan
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/916b9c659c0edbca4d5645c8485865955f449cb5.png[/img]

So I got this email yesterday from a beta tester friend and I know he is a great supporter and expert of Napoli FC. So I thought "Pity that there are no Napoli references in Football Drama" and then "It's so easy to change teams because all the configurations are not hard coded" and then [b]"Wow its all already built for... modding!"[/b].

So then I woke up with the full plan: in the game first development patch after release (after the inevitable first release day patches of panic) I will add (only for desktop versions) a check at startup for a folder of customizations - if enough people ask for it.

You will be able to mod all the team's features, and also the commentary, and even the set of cards and their consequences! Because it is all in CSV files.
Together with that, I will need to add in the app settings:
- Show the mod's folder path.
- Enable a "no personal narrative" mode so that the narrative will focus on the championship and the surrounding narrative events (meeting the other coach, president and press).

All this is actually feasible because of how Football Drama has been built in order to make it easy to test & debug.

[i]"A mod (short for "modification") is an alteration by players or fans of a video game[1] that changes one or more aspects of a video game, such as how it looks or behaves. Mods may range from small changes and tweaks to complete overhauls, and can extend the replay value and interest of the game."[/i] [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mod_(video_gaming)]Wikipedia.[/url]

notes.title: Football Drama Meetings
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/dcc77b33e9e2efe5784bfd6c35a5351c8cf65288.jpg[/img]
This illustration is part of one of Football Drama's finale, and it shows how we are closing its development.

Towards Football Drama's release, and also following it, we have a list of events where we will present previews and materials about the game. here is a (probably partial) calendar.

July: Beta release (English only).

July / August: Three songs from the soundtrack will be released as a preview.

August 20-22: Football Drama presented to the press at [url=https://www.gamescom.global/]Gamescom Cologne[/url]. We will also pitch the nex game (still about sports storytelling).

September 14: We will talk about "Videogames and popular culture" in Ferrara Italy at the[url=https://ivipro.it/it/ivipro-days-2019/] IVPro event[/url]. 

Sept. 24: Football Drama release in 8 languages (EN ITA FR DE PT CH ES) on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/876190/Football_Drama/]Steam[/url], Apple Store, [url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.openlab.footballdrama]Google Play[/url]. The development team will stream on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/876190/Football_Drama/]Steam[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMxaHDEKFfnLMJ5fSxNpKRA]YouTube[/url], [url=https://www.twitch.tv/peterpunkard]Twitch[/url] and [url=https://www.facebook.com/footballDramaGame]Facebook[/url], showing game play, tricks, secret references, playing the soundtrack and chatting with friends and enemies about football, videogames and storytelling. So yes in practice it's a party.

Oct.  10-13: We will talk about Football Drama's development at the [url=https://www.internetfestival.it/]Internet Festival Pisa[/url].

November 8-10 At the [url=https://gamehappens.com/]Game Happens conference[/url] in Genoa (Italy) we will talk about "Changing Sports Storytelling", i.e. about Football Drama's (and the following game) approach to sports storytelling.

So we hope to meet you digitally or in person and get your feedback. Thank you!
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/c7517047686ddb7fdad76d3aa9f32f63b149a3c2.png[/img]

notes.title: Towards 1.0 (September 24th)
notes.notes:
So Football Drama launch date is getting closer, and we are working on it as a perfectly out-of-tune orchestra \o/

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/697b83fb06972e6549e07eb99b99b2f0b0f4076c.jpg[/img]

This is us, at our recent and actually only team meeting and yes, you surely should not trust these guys. Ok, now is there any work getting done? Let's see.

SOUNDTRACK
Football Drama has an original soundtrack by Marta Ascari which will be purchasable separately or as a bundle, also to be released on September 24th. It includes also the song finale that is magicawondrous.
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?list=PLxkBKO9Fy4gpotxOusIjgolD_Fsmxpq8w&v=lh3wt0sQ2xU]Here is a video[/url] of one of the last dialogues with the new soundtrack.

TRANSLATIONS
We are very happy that Football Drama will be published in (at least) seven languages! All telling wildly different stories!

GAMESCOM
Football Drama will be presented in its final version [url=https://www.gamescom.global/]at Gamescom in Cologne[/url] in August (we will be there from August 20th until the 22nd), and we will also have a concept for what will follow. Friends? Journalists? Publishers? Enemies? Meet us there!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/04592ff0cb6b0880080d00025ababe7fb71901b8.png[/img]

notes.title: Football Drama's narrative is getting depth
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33228816/fa9698c02323a7931e790f149e3fe33a3f0f606f.png[/img]

Development of Football Drama is progressing focusing on the last missing core part, the narrative and its interaction with the weekly matches.

The public demos we gave so far only had a small fraction of the narrative, and so our focus in presentations were the weekly matches. The plot is now completed and is progressively getting formalized in dialogues and code. 

We are also further refining the dialogues user interface behaviors and layouts, with a more dynamic usage of the camera.

You find in the images some new characters, layouts and dialogue' structure.
